title: The Adventures of Philip Marlowe
paragraphs: Canonical U.S. Marlowe radio series plus a frozen GRH research container that also preserves cross-show adaptations, BBC novel dramatizations, biographies/intros, and a 2000 documentary.

GRH documents the program through NBC / Van Heflin (June 17, 1947 to September 9, 1947) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], CBS / Gerald Mohr (September 26, 1948 to September 29, 1950) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], CBS summer return (July 7, 1951 to September 15, 1951) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and BBC Chandler adaptations (September 26, 1977 to January 16, 1978) on [[org|org.deepv2.f713a484394d0d32|BBC Radio]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Raymond Chandler (creator on 91 recordings and author on 4 recordings), [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]] (performer on 85 recordings), Norman Macdonnell (producer on 71 recordings, director on 69 recordings, composer on 1 recording, conductor on 1 recording, performer on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording), Roy Rowan (announcer on 71 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Richard Aurandt (music on 45 recordings, composer on 24 recordings, conductor on 23 recordings, and performer on 2 recordings), Gene Levitt (writer on 70 recordings), and Robert Mitchell (writer on 70 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, private detective work, blackmail and coercion, missing persons and disappearances, jewelry and valuable objects, and Los Angeles and Southern California.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Raymond Chandler literary origin, Postwar Los Angeles hard-boiled radio context, BBC revival of Chandler novels, and Radio Detectives Marlowe retrospective.
